title: Baggage-aware hop envelope + lightweight instrumentation for async workers
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Introduce a compact, hop-by-hop trace envelope and baggage-aware sampling hooks for our language SDKs and middleware to improve end-to-end trace continuity through async worker queues and serverless hop chains. The goal is to reduce orphaned spans and incorrect attribution when requests traverse buffering layers (pub/sub, job queues, webhooks) while keeping per-request header size and SDK runtime overhead minimal. This ticket implements the protocol changes, SDK helpers, and a low-cost server-side ingress filter that reconstructs context and enforces sampling decisions based on per-customer retention rules.
acceptance_criteria: A compact envelope format is defined and documented (<= 256 bytes) and approved by security
SDK adapters for Node, Go, and Python can encode/decode the envelope and attach baggage fields declared in our privacy registry
Server-side ingress reconstructs context for 99.9% of sampled traces for test job pipelines (10k messages/min) without increasing P95 request latency by >2ms
Sampler hooks respect explicit user-declared 'no-propagate' baggage and do not persist sensitive keys
End-to-end trace examples (HTTP -> pubsub -> worker -> DB) appear as a single trace in the tracing backend for canary tenant
Unit and integration tests cover header corruption, re-ordering, and truncated envelope cases
tasks: Design envelope wire format and field prioritization (owner: Marco)
Add encode/decode helpers to Node SDK and middleware for express/fastify
Implement lightweight queue adapter for NATS/SQS that preserves envelope across retries
Extend runtime ingress filter to validate and stitch hop envelopes into traces
Add baggage privacy registry and enforcement rules to SDK (denylist + hash-only policy)
Write integration test harness that replays logged events through worker pipeline
Prepare migration guide and rollout plan with canary on internal dev tenants
